day.note: Blair's Sphinx claim can't be checked, and Casey, Ellis and Drew all point at Blair. Alex's Eagle claim is consistent with the table. Calling CAW now makes three and starts the vote on Blair.

Alex.note: I'm the Mouser with Blair as my Meowfia partner. Visiting Ellis to learn their role, since Ellis has been a consistent Owl-claimer and matters for the day.

Blair.note: As Sphinx I learn the Farm roles (Falcon, Hawk, Owl, Tit). I'll choose Hawk and visit the player who is the Hawk to learn who they are.

Casey.note: I'm Farm as the Owl. Drew was Meowfia last round and threw nothing at Finley, so I'll visit Drew to see what animals came to them.

Drew.note: As the Tit I'll visit a player and guess their role for a chance at an egg. No strong read yet, so I'll try Casey as Pigeon.

Ellis.note: As Falcon I learn who my target visited, and I gain an egg if they visited no one. I have no read yet, so I'll pick Drew at random.

Finley.note: As the Hawk I visit one player and gain an egg if they are Meowfia. I have no reads this round, so I'll pick Drew.

events.text: Animals that visited Drew: Falcon, Hawk.

Alex.feeling: I'm Meowfia with Blair, and the table is about to vote Blair out, so I'm trying to keep my own cover while my partner is in danger.

Blair.feeling: Tense and lopsided: I'm Meowfia with Alex, and the Farm side has lined up its claims well, so I'm likely to be voted out and the round is hard to salvage.

Casey.feeling: Tense but clearer than before: Blair's shifting claims and dodges make them look like the cat, though Alex's silence early on still bugs me.

Drew.feeling: Round 3 feels tense but readable: Blair's unverifiable Sphinx claim is the main suspect, and Casey's Owl claim is the one I'd still watch.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 is tense because Blair's Sphinx claim can't be checked, and the table is converging on a vote against Blair.

Finley.feeling: Blair's Sphinx claim doesn't match the visit Blair described, and Casey and Drew's stories fit together, so the vote on Blair feels likely right but is still a guess.

Alex.note: Blair is my Meowfia partner, and the table is voting Blair, so a Farm player is unlikely to be eggsecuted. My stake only banks at 2x if my target is the Farm player eggsecuted, so I'll throw nothing and keep all cards.

Blair.note: Four players have voted on me, so I'm eggsecuted regardless. Throw nothing at Finley to keep my cards.

Casey.note: Blair is the table's consensus target and my read too. I'll throw my two high cards, H12 and D6, at Blair as my stake.

Drew.note: Blair is my confident Meowfia read this round, so I'll throw my two highest cards at Blair to bank them if I'm right.

Ellis.note: Blair's Sphinx claim is unverified and Blair dodged, so I'll throw at Blair. I'll risk only my lower cards and keep the 13 as a floor.

Finley.note: Blair is the table's consensus target and has dodged twice. I'll throw at Blair with a moderate stake and keep my high cards.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle line "lay an egg for every visitor they had" was ambiguous, since "they" could mean the Eagle or its target. That misreading drove most of the day arguments in rounds 1 and 2.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was fun: Blair kept misreading the Eagle rule, and the table caught it and voted them out. It was a good read on the table's logic.
Alex.change: I would reword the Eagle card to say "for every visitor to the player it visits" so the egg counting is unambiguous.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I claimed a false Eagle visit as Meowfia and then threw nothing at Drew, leaving my cards unused. I should have been more careful about lying about my visit, and I should have thrown at the Farm target I suspected instead of staying silent.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle rule was the most confusing: Finley and I both read "lay an egg for every visitor they had" differently, and that confusion drove a lot of the day debate. Also, the Sphinx's claimed Farm-role lookup was hard to verify without a clear Storyteller reminder.
Blair.fun: Watching the table build a case against me in round 1 while I was a Mouser with a live Wink was genuinely tense. Getting Alex to collapse and then watching Finley and Ellis argue the Eagle math was great table theatre.
Blair.change: I would make the Eagle and similar visitor-count wording unambiguous on the card, so players don't spend the day arguing rules instead of reading each other.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I used my Wink on Alex, a Farm player, which removed a Farm voice but did not help my side. I would hold the Wink and stay quiet instead, since Alex's claim was not a real threat to Meowfia.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's rule was easy to misread: several players, including Blair, read "lay an egg for every visitor they had" as counting visits the Eagle made rather than visits it received. Round 1's Alex +2 also got tangled in that same confusion.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when Finley and Ellis caught Blair's misread of the Eagle rule and the table voted Blair out, which turned on a single clear argument.
Casey.change: Print the exact wording of each animal's ability in the dawn report, or let players check the rule text, so visit-counting disputes stop turning on memory.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I stayed silent on Alex's Eagle claim and threw at Drew, a Farm player, which wasted my stake. I would instead have thrown at Blair with my low cards, since Blair was Meowfia and my throw would have banked.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle's visitor-count rule was easy to misread, and it caused most of the Round 2 argument. Also, Blair's Round 3 claim as Sphinx could never be checked by the table.
Drew.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: Ellis's Kookaburra read and Blair's Wink-based collapse lined up, and the table voted Blair out together. It felt like the table was reading each other well.
Drew.change: I would make the Eagle rule and the Sphinx's visit result more explicit in the dawn report, so players can verify claims without arguing over wording.
Drew.regret: In Round 3 I threw two high cards at Blair and banked them, but I also trusted the Farm claims around me too quickly. I would press Alex harder earlier, because Alex was actually Meowfia.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle's wording ("lay an egg for every visitor they had") was ambiguous about whether "they" meant the Eagle or its target, and that caused a lot of argument about the rule.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when Blair kept misreading the Eagle rule, the table caught the contradiction and Farm voted Blair out, which was satisfying to unravel.
Ellis.change: Spell out the Eagle and other visitor-counting rules in the role text so players don't have to argue over what "they" means.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I accepted Alex's Eagle claim too quickly, even though Alex was the Mouser. I would press Alex harder on what their visit showed instead of letting the vote move to Blair.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's rule: "lay an egg for every visitor they had" was easy to misread as counting visitors to the Eagle itself, and Blair's repeated misreading of it caused real confusion in round 2.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when Blair kept insisting the Eagle counted visits on the Eagle, and I held firm and got the table to vote Blair out.
Finley.change: Put the animals' exact visitor-counting wording in the dawn reports so players can check claims like the Eagle's without arguing over the rule.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw only at Blair and never pressed Alex, who was also Meowfia and whose "visited Blair, saw no visitors" claim I accepted without checking; I would have split my pressure onto Alex too.

review.title: Blair Always Loses
review.headline: Blair was a cat all three rounds, and the table voted them out each time.
review.summary: Blair was Meowfia in every round, and the Farm majority eggsecuted them every time. Round 1 had a Wink kill and a muddled Eagle argument. Rounds 2 and 3 were quick pile-ons built on rule misreadings and unverifiable claims. Ellis won by banking big stakes on the winning side each round, while Blair finished with 9.

rounds.recap: Ellis, as Kookaburra, learned Blair was the Mouser and said so on day one. Blair used the Wink on Alex mid-day, which made Blair look even guiltier. Four Farm players threw at Blair and the round ended quickly.

Blair claimed Mouser truthfully and said their visit caused Finley's Eagle +1. Everyone told Blair they had the Eagle rule wrong. Drew, the other cat, mostly stayed out of it and threw nothing. Blair was voted out.

Four Farm claims (Tit, Falcon, Hawk, Owl) matched each other around Drew. Blair claimed Sphinx and Alex claimed Eagle, so only those two were left unconfirmed. Alex's fake Eagle claim could not be checked. The table went for Blair, who was quiet and whose claim was uncheckable. Alex was never seriously suspected.

highlights.text: Blair winked Alex in broad daylight, and Drew immediately cited the Wink as proof Blair was Meowfia.
Blair told the truth as Mouser, but the Eagle-rule argument became a pile-on against them.
Alex claimed Eagle, the animal the app had shown as not in play, so it couldn't be checked, and Alex escaped suspicion.
Tit, Falcon, Hawk and Owl claims interlocked around Drew, leaving the two quiet players as obvious suspects.

confusions.what: Said an Eagle gains eggs per visitor to the Eagle. The card says per visitor to the Eagle's target. Alex's +2 was valid.
Agreed with Blair's wrong Eagle reading and doubted Alex.
Said Owl and Eagle visits on Casey contradicted Casey's unchanged nest, then withdrew it. Those visits don't change the target's nest.
Insisted again that Finley's +1 came from Blair's visit to Finley, repeating the Eagle misreading.
Their Falcon, Owl and Hawk reads cleared Drew, but their later suspicion of Blair rested on 'Sphinx doesn't match the visit Blair described.' That was not a real contradiction.

worked: Eagle, Owl and Falcon visit reports let Farm cross-check claims. Round 3's interlocking claims around Drew made a satisfying puzzle.
Cross-checking nest sizes against claims worked. Casey's +1 and Alex's +2 in round 1 were real evidence.
The Mouser's Wink created a real decision and a dramatic moment in round 1, even though it backfired.
The stake and score rules gave real choices. Ellis's high throws on the winning side decided the game.
problems: Meowfia lost all three rounds, and Blair was eggsecuted every time. With 2 cats among 6 and a majority vote, Farm wins easily. Consider giving Meowfia more tools, or a bonus for surviving a round.
The Eagle rule wording is easy to misread. It caused two long arguments and one wrongful pile-on. Reword it, for example 'visit a player; gain an egg for each player who visited them.'
The 'safe animal not in play' shown to Meowfia is too strong when it is unverifiable. Alex's Eagle claim in round 3 was fully safe. Consider limiting it or making it checkable.
Day talk was repetitive and converged early. Most players just agreed with each other and called CAW. The 4-beat structure with few real conflicts gave little tension.

Cats rarely used their night information well. Casey and Drew often threw nothing or stayed quiet, and no Meowfia stake ever banked, so Meowfia scored almost nothing. The 2x Meowfia stake is irrelevant in practice.
